 Local agencies react to possible cuts to SNAP 
 By Madison Lisowski and Kayleigh Hunter-Gasperini Published : Nov. 10, 2026 at 4:59 PM EST | Updated : seconds ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SPRINGFIELD, Mass. (WGGB/WSHM) - Local agencies in Western Mass. are reacting Tuesday night after the Trump administration proposed a rule that would cut food stamp benefits otherwise known as SNAP benefits. 
 The move would affect over 6.3 million people, including an estimated 1.8 million children who would lost eligibility for free school lunches. 
 Only low income households that receive cash assistance through Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) would now automatically qualify for SNAP. TANF is a federally funded, state run financial and support assistance program. 
 The goal of the move is to save money by curbing SNAP spending. The Trump administration has cited several concerns about waste and SNAP fraud and they say the change could save about $44.6 billion by 2030. 
 The Food Bank of Western Mass. is now responding, saying in part “The Food Bank of Western Massachusetts strongly opposes the Trump administration’s proposal to restrict broad-based categorical eligibility for SNAP, a change that could strip food assistance from millions of people nationwide ... Further restricting access to SNAP will deepen hardship for families, and place additional pressure our region’s food assistance network.”
 The public has 30 days to comment on the proposed rule that states it would “preserves benefits for the truly needy.”
 Western Mass News has reached out to the Massachusetts Department of Transitional Assistance and the governor’s office and is waiting to hear back.
